title: Two-Parameter Loading of an Elastoplastic Multiply Connected Rod
content: The elastoplastic torsion and tension of a prismatic bar featuring a multiply connected circular cross-section with five symmetrically arranged holes are studied and analysed in this issue. The relevance of the problem is determined by the fact that internal contours alter the flow of shear stresses, intensify local gradients in the ligaments, and lead to a non-uniform development of plastic zones. Two-parameter loading is considered in the work. The findings demonstrate that, under two-parameter loading, equivalent stress fields and effective torsional stiffness are heavily influenced by the loading sequence, highlighting the need to account for hole geometry, plastic flow, and load history in perforated bar analysis. The obtained results confirm the need to account jointly for the hole geometry, plastic flow, and loading history when analysing perforated rods.
